extracted.intended_audience: prospective applicants to the Bread Loaf Environmental Writers' Conference / Bread Loaf Writers' Conferences
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for submitting a writing sample as part of an application to the Bread Loaf Environmental Writers' Conference, specifying allowed genres, length limits, formatting, labeling, and exclusions. Applies to fiction, nonfiction, and poetry submissions and notes post-acceptance procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication status / strongest work
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants should send their strongest work not yet published in a book form, though submitting writing that has previously appeared in anthologies or journals is acceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer work that best represents the applicant; previously-published-in-journals/anthologies is allowed but not work already published in book form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prose length limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants should submit a manuscript of current work up to 4,000 words of fiction or nonfiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may include one or more stories as long as the total number of pages is within the 4,000-word limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetry length limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants should submit up to eight pages of poetry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A poem can exceed one page, as long as the complete manuscript submission is within the eight-page limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript identification
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant’s name and a page number must appear on each sheet of the manuscript. (For example: YourLastName, p.1.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include this header/footer on every page to ensure work is identifiable and pages stay in order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prose formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Prose manuscripts must be double-spaced with 12 pt. font and margins of at least 1.25”. The total word count should be noted at the top of the first page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use standard readable formatting (12 pt font, double-spaced, minimum 1.25" margins); include total word count prominently on page one.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetry formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Poetry manuscripts should have 12 pt. font and can be single-spaced or double-spaced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not squeeze more than one poem to a page; format poems with natural spacing and allow poems to run past one page if needed, while keeping total submission ≤ eight pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Labeling of piece type
rubrics_metrics.description: Please include a short note to let readers know if the piece is a short story, an excerpt from a novel or nonfiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly indicate whether the submission is a complete short piece or an excerpt to give readers context for evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Synopsis for excerpts
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts excerpted from a longer project should include a one-page synopsis placed at the back of the piece.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a one-page synopsis after the excerpt so readers understand the broader project and how the excerpt fits into it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excluded genres/types
rubrics_metrics.description: Please do not send children’s or young adult literature, coauthored work, or self-help literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions in these categories will not be accepted; ensure your sample falls within permitted adult-oriented fiction, nonfiction, or poetry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replacement manuscript opportunity
rubrics_metrics.description: Those accepted will have an opportunity to send a replacement manuscript for workshop critique.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If accepted to the conference, applicants may replace their application sample with another manuscript to be used in workshop sessions.
